approach: Read the slope of the displacement-time graph for the sign of velocity, and its curvature for the sign of acceleration.

steps.text: At t = t₁ the curve is rising toward the crest, so the slope is positive, meaning velocity is positive.
At t = t₁ the curve still bends downward there, curving over toward the crest, so acceleration is negative even though the particle is still moving forward.
At t = t₂ the curve is falling after the crest, so the slope is negative, meaning velocity is negative.
At t = t₂ the curve is still bending downward there, falling ever faster (this is before the point where the curve flattens out further along), so acceleration is also negative.

final_answer.value: At t = t₁: velocity is positive, acceleration is negative. At t = t₂: velocity is negative, acceleration is negative.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming acceleration is positive at t₁ just because the particle is moving forward is wrong; a forward-moving particle that is slowing down as it nears the crest has negative acceleration.
